answers.core: Yes, This is a problem that comes up in tons of projects, and makes Godot more intuitive to new users.
answers.workaround:
Examples of workarounds and why they aren't effective
* Parenting each node so that `Pass` will let the current sibling nodes also read the mouse.
This is not a very modifiable or readable approach. This doesn't use parenting for it's intended purpose, and in the case of multiple UI systems acting in unison, it isn't always possible.

* Reading mouse data in `_process`
Reading mouse data in process loses handling of the mouse. As a concrete example, I don't want to trigger `mouse_entered` on the bottom control node if the user is just mousing over the button.

* Adding corner control nodes
This works in this simple example, but it doesn't expand, to fix the problem as a whole. Again, it doesn't work if multiple UI systems are working in unison. It also doesn't work if there are multiple layers that want this functionality.

title: Rework mouse_filter system to be more flexible and intuitive
